{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mn-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"339c245fae46cb23bd5e33e1ef06814527244d6a71cbd40b6f2ddfdfd8eb41e5","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mn-class-d:lineage:60","source_registry_sha256":"960e2daa314aff60b32f5124e42324d79615ce2a3ea953a336216b4593c0c910","source_liveness_sha256":"0b70283fc58b1f8ea1822994a92e3ce7ff4b722004376a9cd819180969b6fe1e"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Impaired driving confusables and continuation facts","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: the alcohol concentration numbers, the two breath tests, offense-by-offense penalties, interlock and underage rules, commercial license losses, alcohol elimination, choices, and cannabis packaging","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: the alcohol concentration numbers, the two breath tests, offense-by-offense penalties, interlock and underage rules, commercial license losses, alcohol elimination, choices, and cannabis packaging
Confusable pairs among the impaired driving numbers and penalties, followed by continuation facts; each block ties to one manual page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec14-R01 | anchor: A01
Drinking and driving is a serious problem in Minnesota, and alcohol use is strongly linked to how severe traffic crashes are. [A01]
Why it matters: group alcohol and crashes; the yearly death figures are dynamic.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec14-R02 | anchor: A01
Drug impairment is as dangerous as alcohol impairment, and drugs can cause drowsiness and slow your response to driving conditions, leading to crashes, arrest, fines and jail. [A01]
Why it matters: group drugs; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec14-R03 | anchor: A02
The liver removes 95 percent of alcohol by oxidation, and the rest leaves through breathing, sweating and urination. [A02]
Why it matters: group alcohol elimination; prereq for the wait rule.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec14-R04 | anchor: A02
Alcohol affects people very differently because of age, gender, body weight, mood, food intake, metabolism and genetics, and even the same person can react differently from one occasion to the next. [A02]
Why it matters: group alcohol effects; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec14-R05 | anchor: A02
Alcohol affects men and women differently, partly because men usually carry more muscle, and muscle takes alcohol into the bloodstream less readily than fat does. [A02]
Why it matters: group alcohol effects; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec14-R06 | anchor: A03
Alternatives to driving impaired include a designated driver who does not drink, a taxi or rideshare, a ride from a friend or relative, staying overnight, and taking the keys from an impaired friend. [A03]
Why it matters: group lower-risk choices; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec14-R07 | anchor: A03
The DWI and implied consent laws also apply to off-road recreational vehicles and motorboats. [A03]
Why it matters: group DWI scope; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec14-R08 | anchor: A03
An officer may ask for a test when you are under arrest for DWI, refuse or fail a preliminary breath test, or are in an alcohol-related crash causing injury, damage or death. [A03]
Why it matters: group testing; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec14-R09 | anchor: A03
Social drinking frequently leads to impaired driving, and because alcohol impairs judgment you should decide how you will get home before you start drinking. [A03]
Why it matters: group lower-risk choices; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec14-R10 | anchor: A03
Three different limits appear on this page: 0.08 percent for most drivers, 0.04 percent for commercial drivers, and 0.04 percent for any driver whose errors an officer proves were caused by alcohol. [A03]
Why it matters: group legal limits; confusable general versus commercial versus proven-error limit; difficulty high.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec14-R11 | anchor: A03
The roadside preliminary breath test helps the officer judge your alcohol level before arrest, while the blood, breath or urine test after arrest is the one used as evidence. [A03]
Why it matters: group breath tests; confusable preliminary versus evidentiary test; difficulty high.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec14-R12 | anchor: A03
A preliminary breath test can help a driver who seems intoxicated but is not, because some medical conditions look like intoxication, and officers get medical help for drivers who are ill. [A03]
Why it matters: group breath tests; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec14-R13 | anchor: A04
Each impaired driving offense carries criminal penalties in addition to administrative sanctions, depending on the arrest situation, prior violations and criminal record. [A04]
Why it matters: group penalties; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec14-R14 | anchor: A04
Revocation minimums climb by offense: at least ninety days for a first offense, at least one year for a second within 10 years, and at least three years for a third within 10 years. [A04]
Why it matters: group penalties; confusable first versus second versus third offense; difficulty high.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec14-R15 | anchor: A04
Ignition interlock is optional after a first offense, possibly required after a second, and required after a third. [A04]
Why it matters: group interlock; confusable optional versus possible versus required; difficulty high.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec14-R16 | anchor: A04
A third offense can also bring jail or maximum bail with electronic monitoring. [A04]
Why it matters: group penalties; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec14-R17 | anchor: A05
The interlock blocks starting at 0.02 percent, which is lower than both the 0.04 commercial limit and the 0.08 general limit. [A05]
Why it matters: group alcohol numbers; confusable interlock versus legal limits; difficulty high.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec14-R18 | anchor: A05
First-time offenders with an alcohol concentration of 0.16 or above may choose the Ignition Interlock Device Program to regain their driving privileges. [A05]
Why it matters: group interlock; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec14-R19 | anchor: A05
A fourth offense can mean four years without a license, and the license comes back only after rehabilitation and the other reinstatement steps are complete. [A05]
Why it matters: group felony DWI; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec14-R20 | anchor: A05
The legal age to buy and drink alcohol in Minnesota is 21. [A05]
Why it matters: group underage; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec14-R21 | anchor: A05
A commercial license holder loses that license for at least one year on a first offense such as driving any vehicle at 0.08 or more, refusing a blood, breath or urine test, driving under a controlled substance, leaving a crash scene, or using a vehicle for a felony. [A05]
Why it matters: group commercial licenses; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec14-R22 | anchor: A05
If the offense happens in a placarded hazardous materials vehicle the commercial license is lost for at least three years, and a second offense or using a commercial vehicle for a controlled substance felony means permanent loss. [A05]
Why it matters: group commercial licenses; confusable one year versus three years versus permanent; difficulty high.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec14-R23 | anchor: A05
A commercial license holder arrested for impaired driving in a passenger vehicle cannot get a work permit for a commercial vehicle during the withdrawal period. [A05]
Why it matters: group commercial licenses; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec14-R24 | anchor: A06
An opened or partly emptied package of cannabis or hemp-derived products is illegal in a private vehicle on a street or highway unless stored in the trunk or another unoccupied area. [A06]
Why it matters: group cannabis; prereq for the storage rule.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec14-R25 | anchor: A06
When the owner is not in the vehicle, it is still illegal for the owner to keep or allow opened cannabis or hemp-derived packages in it on a street or highway. [A06]
Why it matters: group cannabis; difficulty high.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0099]
